prompt: A poll estimates that $48\%$ of voters support a measure, with a margin of error of $3$ percentage points. Which value of the true population percentage is NOT consistent with this result?
hint: The margin of error creates an interval around the estimate.

hints.text: The margin of error creates an interval around the estimate.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try an easy interval: an estimate of $50\%$ with a margin of $2$ points spans $48\%$ to $52\%$. Build the interval first, then check which value sits outside it.
The interval is $48 \pm 3$, so from $45\%$ to $51\%$.

learningObjective: Build and use a margin-of-error interval.
explanation: The estimate plus or minus the margin gives the plausible interval: $48 - 3 = 45$ to $48 + 3 = 51$.
Choices A, B, and C all lie within $[45, 51]$ and are therefore consistent with the poll.
$53\%$ lies outside, so it is not supported.

alternativeExplanations.title: What shrinks the margin
steps: A larger sample narrows the margin of error; a smaller one widens it.
The margin reflects sampling variability only — it does not account for a biased sampling method.
A badly-drawn sample can have a tiny margin of error and still be completely wrong about the population.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: 45% looks suspicious because it sits exactly on the boundary — but the interval INCLUDES its endpoints.
Build the interval first: 45 to 51, endpoints in. Only then scan the choices for the value outside; 53% is the lone stranger.
